summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of AML status post allogeneic stem cell transplant and extensive chronic graft-versus-host disease was admitted for worsening dyspnea, cough, and low-grade fever. He was found to have E. coli bacteremia, likely from an unclear source, and was treated with antibiotics including ertapenem. His acute kidney injury, which peaked due to multiple nephrotoxic factors including medications and volume depletion, improved with supportive care and a dose of rasburicase. Heart failure was managed with diuresis and transition from metoprolol to carvedilol. His ruxolitinib was temporarily reduced, and sirolimus was held. He stabilized over 17 days, with resolution of infection, improved renal function, and controlled symptoms, and was discharged home on oral antibiotics, heart failure medications, and immunosuppressants with close outpatient follow-up planned.
problems: Acute on chronic systolic (congestive) heart failure
